title: Taj Mahal
blurb: A detailed schematic model of the Taj Mahal complex in Agra, India, the 17th-century Mughal mausoleum commissioned by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal. This deeper cut opens up the full walled complex in 170 named parts: the Yamuna riverfront terrace, the marble plinth and 33 m pishtaq arches, the drum and onion dome with its 9.6 m gilded finial, four 43.02 m minarets shown tier by tier, the octagonal burial chamber with its cenotaphs and marble jali screen, the 23.07 m great gate, the mosque and jawab, the 296.31 m charbagh garden with its water channels and fountains, the jilaukhana forecourt, and the Saheli Burj subsidiary tombs.

systems.name: Riverfront Terrace
systems.description: The 300 m riverfront platform on the Yamuna and its boundary walls, the foundation of the whole composition.

systems.name: Mausoleum Base
systems.description: The 6 m marble plinth and the main tomb block with its four 33 m pishtaq arches, opened arch by arch.

systems.name: Dome Cluster
systems.description: The 12 m drum, the 23 m onion dome, the 9.6 m gilded finial, and the roof chhatris, split into their layers.

systems.name: Minarets
systems.description: Four 43.02 m marble minarets at the plinth corners, each shown tier by tier with its balconies and crowning chhatri.

systems.name: Interior Chamber
systems.description: The octagonal burial chamber with its cenotaphs, the marble jali screen, and the lower tomb.

systems.name: Great Gate
systems.description: The 23.07 m red sandstone gateway, Darwaza-i rauza, closing the garden on the south.

systems.name: Mosque
systems.description: The red sandstone mosque west of the tomb, with its three domes, prayer bays, and mihrab.

systems.name: Jawab
systems.description: The eastern mirror of the mosque, built for architectural symmetry rather than worship.

systems.name: Charbagh Garden
systems.description: The 296.31 m square four-part garden with sunken parterres and raised walkways.

systems.name: Waterworks
systems.description: The 120 m water channels, the central tank with its fountains, and the gravity-fed supply system.

systems.name: Jilaukhana Forecourt
systems.description: The entrance forecourt south of the great gate: bazaar streets, enclosure walls, and the attendants quarters, the worldly side of the complex.

systems.name: Subsidiary Tombs
systems.description: The Saheli Burj: two mirror-image tombs at the southern corners of the forecourt, conceived as miniature replicas of the main complex.

explanations.terrace platform: A 300 m long, 111.89 m deep platform, 8.7 m high, on the banks of the Yamuna, carrying the mausoleum, minarets, mosque, and jawab. Its faces mix dark and light sandstone patterns.
explanations.yamuna-side open front: The complex is enclosed by crenellated red sandstone walls on three sides, with the river side left open to the Yamuna.
explanations.west boundary wall: Crenellated red sandstone wall closing the west side of the riverfront terrace.
explanations.east boundary wall: Crenellated red sandstone wall closing the east side of the riverfront terrace.
explanations.tahkhana river rooms: A galleried suite of rooms under the terrace opening toward the river, used by the imperial retinue during celebrations; the room layout is schematic.
explanations.river ghat steps: Steps descending from the riverfront edge of the terrace to the Yamuna, the ceremonial water gate of the complex. The steps are schematic.
explanations.terrace corner chhatris: Open pillared kiosks marking the riverfront corners of the terrace. Their positions and sizes are schematic.
explanations.marble plinth: A 6 m high square plinth with 95.5 m sides, faced in white marble from Makrana, raising the tomb above the terrace. Its top carries an interlocking pattern of octagonal marble pieces set into four-pointed red sandstone stars.
explanations.main octagonal block: A multi-chambered cube with chamfered corners forming an eight-sided structure, 56.9 m square with long sides near 57.3 m.
explanations.south access stairs, west flight: One of two partly covered flights of stairs on the south side of the platform, facing the garden; they provide the only access from ground level up to the mausoleum. Stair placement is schematic.
explanations.south access stairs, east flight: One of two partly covered flights of stairs on the south side of the platform, facing the garden; they provide the only access from ground level up to the mausoleum. Stair placement is schematic.
explanations.dome drum: A 12 m high cylindrical drum with an 18.4 m inner diameter, carrying the outer dome.
explanations.drum rope moulding: An ornamental moulding with a twisted rope design in the intermediate zone between the drum and the dome.
explanations.drum arcade niches: Arched niches ringing the drum below the dome, lightening its mass. The niche forms are schematic.
explanations.outer onion dome: A 23 m high marble onion dome, 17.7 m in diameter, built as a larger outer shell over the inner dome.
explanations.dome lotus base: A lotus flower design ringing the base of the dome, matching the lotus ornament on the domes; the petal forms are schematic.
explanations.inner false dome: A smaller separate interior dome over the burial chamber, decorated with a sun motif; it rises about 35 m from the ground.
explanations.inner dome sun motif: The sun motif decorating the smaller interior dome, the luminous counterpart to the crescent on the outer finial. The motif geometry is schematic.
explanations.gilded finial: A 9.6 m high finial of stacked orbs on a shaft, originally gold and replaced by a gilded bronze copy in the early 19th century. A 4.6 m gold shield that once covered it was carried off in the 18th century Jat despoliation.
explanations.crescent moon: The finial is topped by a moon, a typical Islamic motif whose horns point heavenward, and it forms the tamga, the seal of the Mughal Empire.
explanations.octagonal burial chamber: The main inner chamber is an octagon with 7.3 m sides, entered from each face, with walls about 25 m high.
explanations.interior pishtaq arches, lower tier: The lower tier of eight pishtaq arches lining the chamber walls; the arch forms are schematic.
explanations.interior pishtaq arches, upper tier: The upper tier of eight pishtaq arches lining the chamber walls, the four central upper arches forming viewing balconies; the arch forms are schematic.
explanations.mumtaz cenotaph: The cenotaph of Mumtaz Mahal on a 1.5 by 2.5 m marble base at the center of the chamber, aligned north-south with the head to the north and the face turned west toward Mecca.
explanations.shah jahan cenotaph: The cenotaph of Shah Jahan on a larger base to the west, the only asymmetric element in the chamber; the pen box on top denotes a male tomb.
explanations.lower tomb chamber: The plain rectangular basement chamber shell holding the actual graves, below the cenotaphs, with an undecorated coved ceiling.
explanations.actual graves: The plain graves of Mumtaz Mahal and Shah Jahan in the basement chamber, below the ornamental cenotaphs. The slab forms are schematic.
explanations.great gate body: The great gate, Darwaza-i rauza, measures 41.2 by 34 m and stands 23.07 m high, built of red sandstone with white marble accents.
explanations.gate central arch: A recessed two-story central arch, 33 m high and 19 m wide, framed in white marble with a triple rope moulding; the frame carries the Daybreak sura in thuluth script and the entry iwan holds muqarnas in red sandstone.
explanations.gate flanking arches: Two pairs of smaller decorative iwans flanking the central arch on each facade; the gate has five iwans per facade and the smaller ones are purely decorative.
explanations.gate calligraphy panels: Black calligraphy inlay panels set into the red sandstone facades; the southern gate inscription invites the soul at rest to return to the Lord at peace.
explanations.gate side chambers: Side chambers of the gate's nine-part plan; the internal layout is schematic.
explanations.gate internal dome: The large central space of the gate is crowned by an internal dome that receives no outward expression: external domes were reserved for tombs and mosques. The dome form is schematic.
explanations.gate muqarnas vault: Honeycomb muqarnas vaulting in red sandstone inside the entry iwan. The vault geometry is schematic.
explanations.mosque pishtaq: The great arched prayer front of the mosque, facing the mausoleum.
explanations.mosque mihrab: The prayer niche in the mosque's west wall marking the direction of Mecca; the jawab has inlaid floors but no mihrab. The niche form is schematic.
explanations.jawab pishtaq: The great arched front of the jawab, mirroring the mosque for architectural symmetry.
explanations.charbagh garden platform: The charbagh is a 296.31 m square garden divided into four quadrants, each quarter further split into 16 sunken parterres.
explanations.charbagh south enclosure wall: Crenellated red sandstone enclosure wall on the garden's south side, pierced by the great gate.
explanations.charbagh west enclosure wall: Crenellated red sandstone enclosure wall on the garden's west side; the inner sides of the complex walls carry columned arcades with chhatris and the Music House, modeled schematically.
explanations.charbagh east enclosure wall: Crenellated red sandstone enclosure wall on the garden's east side; the inner sides of the complex walls carry columned arcades with chhatris and the Music House, modeled schematically.
explanations.garden tree rows: Avenues of trees line the garden; early accounts describe roses, daffodils, and fruit trees in abundance, and the British later replanted cypresses. Tree positions are schematic.
explanations.khiyaban walkways, north-south: Raised walkways edging the north-south water channels, the main promenades of the garden.
explanations.khiyaban walkways, east-west: Raised walkways edging the east-west water channels, the main promenades of the garden.
explanations.temporary burial enclosure: A low walled enclosure in the western garden near the riverfront terrace marks where Mumtaz Mahal's body rested temporarily after its arrival from Burhanpur. The enclosure form is schematic.
explanations.north-south channel, north reach: The four straight channels of the garden are each 120 m long and 6 m wide, a little shorter than half the garden to leave room for the central fountain.

explanations.central water tank: The raised marble tank al Hawd al-Kawthar with five fountains at the center of the garden.
explanations.tank fountain nozzles: The five fountain nozzles of the raised central tank al Hawd al-Kawthar. Their exact positions are schematic.
explanations.reflecting pool: The long reflecting pool on the north-south axis mirrors the mausoleum.
explanations.channel fountain nozzles: Fountain nozzles set along the water channels, fed by the garden waterworks. The nozzle positions are schematic.
explanations.underground reservoir: The underground reservoir that received Yamuna water through a channel before it was lifted to the aqueduct. The reservoir form and position are schematic.
explanations.aqueduct conduits: Elevated conduits carrying water from the reservoir toward the garden center, feeding the channels and fountains. The conduit route is schematic.
explanations.jilaukhana forecourt: The entrance forecourt south of the great gate, about 124 m deep (153 gaz), where visitors dismounted from horses and elephants and assembled in style before entering the tomb complex.
explanations.east bazaar street: Bazaar street leading from the east gate to the center of the forecourt, lined by colonnades with cusped arches; shops traded here from the construction until 1996, and their tax revenue maintained the complex. The street layout is schematic.

explanations.west saheli burj garden: The small charbagh garden laid out in front of the western Saheli Burj tomb; the planting is schematic.
